Carbon-carbon bonds are formed between malonic acid esters and aldehydes in the Knoevenagel type, while acyloin and benzoin are both commonly synthesized using this type of reaction. Alpha-beta- unsaturated carbonyl compounds and beta-keto esters are the products of two common examples that involve the reaction of two aldehydes or ketones in the first case, and two esters in the second. Identify this type of chemical reaction, examples of which include aldol and Claisen, in which two molecules are covalently bonded to each other with the release of a small molecule.

Ueguchi-Tanada and colleagues discovered the nuclear receptor for this class of molecules that function by degrading DELLA repressor proteins. Their downstream effects include the enhancement of histone H1 kinase activity and expression of mitotic cyclins, consistent with its role in promoting stem elongation. All members of this family are diterpenes derived from an eponymous four-ringed skeleton. They were first identified not in plants but in fungi of the genum Fusarium. Identify this class of plant hormones which, when over-expressed, cause foolish seedling disease.

Trouton's rule states that for a liquid to vaporize, this thermodynamic quantity is approximately equal to 21 times the universal gas constant times the boiling temperature. The virial expansion for this state function is proportional to the square of temperature. This natural function of entropy and pressure is constant in throttling processes, a fact that is exploited in Joule-Thomson cooling. Determined experimentally by measuring the heat associated with a constant-pressure process, identify this thermodynamic potential defined as the internal energy plus the pressure times the volume.

In a rare birth defect, a child is born without this organ and hence develops DiGeorge Syndrome. Removal of it has been used successfully to treat Morvan's Syndrome, which is consequently suspected to be autoimmune in origin. Yongjun Liu identified the function of the Hassall's corpuscles found in the medullae of this gland. In some myasthenia gravis patients, tumors develop in it. It is an endodermic organ, and it atrophies markedly after puberty. Identify this gland of the lymphatic system, responsible for the transformation of lymphocytes into its namesake T-cells.

Its oxygen atoms are arranged in a hexagonal close-pack denser than that of quartz, which accounts for its greater hardness in spite of the fact that its bonds are less covalent than those of quartz. Its fine granular form, when mixed with magnetite, is an industrial abrasive called emery, and it is often used as the grit of sandpaper. Identify this crystalline form of aluminum oxide, the major varieties of which are topaz, sapphire, and ruby, whose Mohs hardness is defined as nine

The Kerr varieties of these objects are defined as exact solutions to the Einstein field equations. The Reissner-Nordström varieties have angular momentum of zero, and if they have zero charge as well, it can be shown that they have constant density, and they are of the Schwarzschild variety. Eternal ones are massless. The Bekenstein-Hawking formula can be used to calculate their entropy. The centrifugal force sometimes reverses direction in the vicinity of these objects. Identify these cosmological objects that emit Hawking radiation, singularities surrounded by event horizons.

Peng and Robinson's is more commonly used than the Dieterici and Bertholet ones, which are examples of the two-parameter type. The Wohl type is useful for its statement in terms of critical values, and one of the most complex is the Beattie-Bridgeman type. "Thermal" types are less common than "Volumetric" types, which include the virial one and which relate the pressure, temperature and volume of a substance. The Ideal Gas Law is perhaps the best-known example of what three-word phrase for a constitutive equation describing a phase of matter under given physical conditions?

In some cases it can arise from pressure applied to the Pacinian corpuscles *, though in the auditory region it is due to cochlear microphonic functioning Its curve reaches the highest point at the overshoot level and shows a very short latent period. Among its characteristics are an absolute or relative refractory period, biphasic occurrence, and obeyance of the all or none law. Its two portions are caused the by influx of sodium ions and efflux of potassium ions and are termed depolarization and repolarization. Electrical signaling occurs as a result of, what excitation phenomenon found in nerve cells?

It reverses itself in Minkowski spaces, while a physical manifestation of this concept is the twin paradox of special relativity. Appearing as a theorem in spaces such as the real numbers and LP spaces where p is greater than or equal to one, the Cauchy-Bunyakovski-Schwartz version is used to determine if x and y, both members of inner product spaces, are linearly dependent. In normed vector spaces, it is defined as the norm of the sum of two vectors x and y is lesser than or equal to the sum of the norms of x and y. Identify this mathematical concept that in its simplest form states given three points A, B and C, the distance from A to C never exceeds the sum of the distances between A and B, and B and C.

The conversion of histidine into this in spoiled food has been cited as a cause of food poisoning. As a neurotransmitter ejected from the posterior hypothalamus, it has a direct affect on wakefulness and sleep, including REM. The four receptors that act on this substance cause a variety of reactions, including regulation release of other neurotransmitters, gastric acid secretion, and activation of certain smooth muscle and endothelial cells, which are related to hives. Also known as 2-(4-imidazolyl)ethylamine, name this chemical involved in local immune responses whose existence has spawned a series of medicines to foil those responses.

Weaker versions of this mathematical statement include the Boolean prime ideal theorem, while concepts requiring it include Tychonoff's theorem, trichotomy involving the cardinal numbers, and that every vector space has a basis. Proofs requiring it are always nonconstructive. The Banach-Tarski paradox, Baire category theorem, well-ordering theorem and Zorn's lemma are all equivalent to, this fundamental assertion that is logically independent of Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory, that states for a set of non-empty sets X, one can select a member from each set in X.

The Schilling test can determine whether the symptoms of deficiency of this vitamin are caused by lack of intrinsic factor. The deficiency, if present, is called pernicious anemia and is traditionally treated via intramuscular injection. The vitamin contains a central cobalt atom surrounded by a corrin ring of nitrogens. It is only produced by bacteria produced in animals, so vegans often turn to fortified yeast extract, which only collects the vitamin when grown in animal excrement. Identify this compound with scientific name cyanocobalamin, the last in the series of B vitamins.

It was first published in a 1921 monograph, although some alternative systems developed by William Holtzman and Wilfred Cassell, respectively, have become accepted. Scoring is done via a namesake scale developed by John Exner, which notes what factor the patient responds to, whether it is form, color, or even the perception of movement. All examinations are done on a one to one basis, and touching or turning any of the ten cards may indicate signs of mental damage. Identify this method of evaluation, named for a Swiss psychologist, which uses inkblots to probe the unconscious mind of the patient.

There are three species of these carnivorous mammals. The mountain variety is found only in South America and the species Nasua nelsoni is confined to Cozumel Island in Central America, while the common or ring-tailed variety ranges throughout the forests of Central and South America. Characterized by elongated snouts and a tail that is held erect when walking, they climb trees in search of birds and lizards, as well as fruit insects and larvae. Name these members of the raccoon family.

It was settled by Angles around 500, first along the Trent Valley. Their first great leader was Penda, who extended his power over Wessex and East Anglia in the mid-7th century. Offa reigned from 757-796 and had a great dike built to protect the western portion of the kingdom from the Welsh. Name this Anglo-Saxon kingdom which eventually succumbed to the Danes and control by Alfred of Wessex in the late 9th century.

In plants, F-actin may play a big role in this process, which can be anticipated by the placement of a ring-shaped structure known as PPB, which may dictate the site that a phragmoplast is eventually guided to. Vesicle trafficking aids in expanding that phragmoplast in order to create a cell plate. In animals, myosin II is a key contractile protein that forms a furrow by pinching or puckering inward at the cell equator. Beginning in anaphase and continuing through telophase, name this process that formally splits a cell with two or more nuclei into two separate cells.

UCLA scientists have suggested that irregularities in the surrounding gas cloud may result from a Neptune-sized planet. It is the brightest star in a constellation that features an epsilon star known as the Double-Double and a Beta star known as Sheliak or Tortoise. Its name comes from an Arabic phrase meaning "the falling vulture" or "stone eagle," and in Chinese mythology, it represents the wife of Altair. In 12000 years it will be the North Star. Name this vertex of the Summer Triangle, the fifth brightest star in the sky and the brightest in Lyra.

It is fabled to have been used to count the size of armies in ancient times. In modern computer applications, it is used to solve simultaneous systems of equations using exact arithmetic and is also applied to random number generation. The theorem has been extended to general rings and in modern parlance it can be stated that given N congruence relations of the form x equals a mod p, where the p's are relatively prime, there exists an integer solution. Name this ancient theorem regarding simultaneous congruences, generally attributed to Sun Zi and Qin Jiushao.

In quantum field theory, it is equivalent to one-loop Feynman diagrams. The idea is originally attributed to Lord Rayleigh, who used it to analyze the propagation of an optical disturbance in a nonuniform medium. In his version, he assumed that the wave number was proportional to the index of refraction. The rigorous mathematical theory of this approximation for linear second-order differential equations was developed by Harold Jeffreys. Name this approximation valid when the potential varies slowly compared to the wave function, a truncated asymptotic series named after three physicists.

He termed the fear of knowing one's self "the Jonah complex," and late in his life he pioneered the study of "transpersonal psychology," which derived a lot of its inspiration from non-Western sources. In a 1968 work he tried to steer people away from what he called "D-perception" and "D-motivation" and Towards a Psychology of Being. Works like Eupsychian Management and Motivation and Personality develop the ideas based on his most revolutionary paradigm, which was introduced to him by his colleague at Brandeis, Kurt Goldstein. This idea posited that persons would be unable to reach their full potential, or self-actualize, without taking care of certain basic necessities. Identify this father of humanistic psychology who developed a pyramidal hierarchy of needs.

It has a flux of about 2720 Janskies at 1 gigahertz, and is expanding at the rate of approximately ten million miles per hour. This rate of expansion is slowing, but whether the rate in the change of the rate of expansion is slowing or not is still under debate. Though one of the brightest radio sources in the sky, it was not discovered until 1947 due to large clouds of interstellar dust between it and us blocking optical observations of it. Believed to be about 350 years old, name this supernova remnant located in one of the circumpolar constellations.

This egg-shaped structure makes up more than 80% of the diencephalon and forms the superolateral walls of the third ventricle. Its name means "inner room" in Greek and in some people its bilateral masses of gray matter are held together by the intermediate mass. Name this gateway to the cerebral cortex which plays a key role in mediating sensation, motor activities, cortical arousal, learning and memory.

That of cows is often taken as a dietary supplement; unlike the normal variety that it replaces, it is yellow and thick. Higher in carbohydrates and protein than the other variety, it is correspondingly lower in fat, and it also contains many helpful antibodies. It is also a mild laxative, which helps prevent jaundice and assists the consumer in delivering the meconium, or first stool. Also called beestings, name this form of breast milk produced in the late hours of pregnancy and immediately after giving birth.

Postulated and studied by astrophysicist J. Richard Gott, these objects are infinitely long and moving at speeds close to the speed of light. Theorized to have formed loops in the early universe, possibly leading to the clumping of matter that led to galaxy formation, they are defects in the fabric of space-time, and are very thin, about the diameter of a proton, but extremely dense. Name these as-yet-unobserved astronomical phenomena that sound a great deal like a 10-dimensional potential theory of everything.

First predicted in the 1960s, in the Standard Model, this particle's namesake field consists of two neutral and one charged component fields. One neutral and the charged component fields are Goldstone variety of its class, which are massless and unphysical. The other neutral component field has a quantum which is this theoretical particle with non-zero mass. Name this hypothetical elementary particle, as of yet undetected, which theoretically permeates the universe and gives mass to all other particles.

Lesser-known ways to form them include metasomatism, retrograde, and hydrothermal. Mineral and textural changes are characteristic when they form. The regional varieties occur in the roots of mountain ranges. Foliation is usually the first aspect evaluated when they are categorized. The contact method of producing them are found in aureoles. Examples of them are marble, quartzite, and slate. Name this type of rock, examples of which include marble, quartzite and slate, which are sedimentary or igneous rocks that have been changed by heat and/or pressure.

The F factor was the first of these to be described, while the col variety of these objects contains genes that produce specific bacteriocins that work against E. Coli. An episome is an example of one of these that can exist whether or not it is integrated into a host's chromosome. Some of these contain genes for pilli, and they can be passed from cell to another during conjugation. Name this small, double stranded type of DNA molecule found in bacteria as well as some fungi and yeast.

One of his earliest accomplishments was to find a simple solution to the Apollonian gasket. His namesake sequence is one whose members become mathematically close as the sequence progresses. His name is applied, with Binet, to a formula to determine the determinant of the product of two non- square matrices; with Euler, to a second order ordinary differential equation of the form x2u'' [x squared u double prime] + bxu' [b u prime] + cu = 0; and, with Maclaurin, to an integral test for convergence of a series. The first person to rigorously prove Taylor's Theorem, name this pioneer and namesake of many theorems of complex analysis.

A mixture of glycerin, methanol, methylene azure and eosin, this type of stain is often used on blood films, bone marrow, and certain parasites. Appearing purple by itself, it stains erythrocytes pink, platelets light pink, leukocytes magenta-purple, and monocyte cytoplasm blue. Name this classical biological stain that is often combined with trypsin to stain chromosomes, producing the namesake G-bands.

Common topologies for these include recurrent and layered feed forward, though more complex varieties of the latter can include units in hidden layers, producing a multilayer perceptron. In order to minimize error in their output, various algorithms such as back propagation and conjugate gradient descent are used to set optimal thresholds and weights, thus training each node. Name this highly parallel type of computation that is used in artificial intelligence and pattern recognition and is inspired by biological systems.

The ground, streamlined, fluted ridge, and transverse ridge types of this phenomenon have low topographic relief. When it results in kettles, the landscape is known as hummocky topography. The end type can become terminal when it remains stationary for a long time, and the recessional type can form around the margin. The lateral type forms at the sides of valley, while the medial type appears as a strip of dirt in the middle of a glacier. Made up of till and glacial outwash, name this accumulation of sediment deposited by a glacier after it melts, not to be confused with eskers.

In organic chemistry, this term refers to the process of separation of enantiomers. In first-order logic, it is an inference algorithm that converts sentences to conjunctive normal form and attempts to find a contradiction by unifying all possible literals. John Alan Robinson gave a derivation of this principle in an Association for Computing Machinery paper on "machine oriented logic," but it is also complete for propositional logic. Give this term that also refers to the number of pixels on a monitor, measured in dots per inch.

A type of them can be used to make inorganic salts soluble in nonpolar organic solvents. That type can exist in an 18-member ring around potassium, a 15-member ring around sodium, or a 12-member ring around lithium. Essential to the formation of Grignard reagents, they can be created by bimolecular dehydration of alcohol or the Williamson synthesis and sometimes exist in the "crown" form. Name this organic compound containing a bond between an oxygen atom and two alkyl groups, whose diethyl form was once a common anesthetic.

His name graces a set of equations, applicable to electromagnetic radiation incident on a dielectric, which determine the ratio of transmitted and reflected electric field amplitude to the initial electric field. He also has a device which makes use of constructive interference, called his "zone plates," and a "number" calculated as the aperture radius squared over the wavelength times distance from the aperture. When that number is approximately equal to 1, his "diffraction" occurs. Name this physicist who also assembled concentric rings of glass into a device useful in lighthouses, known as his "lens."

Dalziel Hammick showed that this process in alpha-trioxymethylene results in polyoxymethylene, which was later used as a commercial polymer. Phenarsazine chloride undergoes it readily, making it useful as a chemical warfare agent, and uranium hexafluoride undergoes it to separate uranium isotopes. The Hortvet device can determine the temperature at which this occurs, and so-called "flowers of sulfur" are created by it. An apophorometer uses it to identify minerals, and hoar crystals always grow by this process. Occurring at temperatures and pressures below the triple point, name this phase exemplified by dry ice, in which a solid changes directly into a gas.

Allgrove's syndrome causes achalasia [a-kuh-LAY-zhuh] and dilation of it, and Zenker's diverticulum and Schatzki's ring are often signs of trauma to it. Boerhaave syndrome is a transmural perforation of it that, like the similar Mallory-Weiss syndrome, can be fatal and usually occurs after forceful emesis. Paterson-Kelly syndrome causes webs to form in it, and ulceration of it named after Barrett causes difficulty swallowing. Name this part of the digestive tube affected by acid reflux disorder, which uses peristalsis to convey boluses of food from the mouth to the stomach.

Donald Knuth [k-nooth] makes one variety of them "dance" in an algorithm for solving pentomino puzzles and the n-queens problem. Their "unrolled" variety contains arrays of elements and their "skip" type allows large numbers of elements to be ignored, improving their linear indexing time. Often containing data-less "sentinels" at their beginning and end, they were created by Simon, Newell, and Shaw for the Information Processing Language, and their representation as blocks and arrows won the latter two a Turing Award. Name this data structure in which each data node contains a pointer to the subsequent data node.

Before a new class, W, was invented for Wolf-Rayet stars, those would have been stars of this class, having broad emission lines in their spectra. For a general star of this class, hydrogen lines are relatively weak, while ionized helium and highly ionized metals are the most prominent lines due to the extreme heat. Naos, in the Puppis constellation, is a star of this type, emitting most of its radiation in the ultra-violet. A main-sequence star of this class would have a violet color, a temperature of around 40,000 Kelvins, and 500,000 times the Sun's luminosity. What is this spectral class, which contains the hottest and brightest stars?

Among those that use it are sugarcane and corn, as well as many others, all characterized by the special leaf anatomy required for this procedure. In the bundle-sheath cells, the Calvin cycle takes place as normal, using the CO2 from malate, sending the carbohydrate product into the vascular system while the excess pyruvate returns to the mesophyll, where it is phosphorylated, forming PEP, which is used to capture carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, allowing the process to repeat. This describes what alternative photosynthetic pathway that allows for spatial separation of the light and dark reactions?

The Nash equilibrium solution to this situation is known as the Bertrand equilibrium. If one of the firms acts as a leader, this produces the Stackelberg equilibrium, in which the output is higher than the original solution to this problem, known as the Cournot equilibrium, whose creator initially had a thought experiment involving access to two natural springs. What is this economic situation, a special case of oligopoly in which only two firms are selling in a market?

The 2, 3, 10, and 11 exons in the pre-mRNA for tropomyosin are spliced out for its expression in this organ. It gives its name to a hormone in Rhodnius secreted by the corpora cardiaca that stimulates ecdysone release, causing molting. Its ingestion by the Fore causes kuru, and when starved, it consumes beta-hydroxybutyrate and acetoacetate. Losing function in the paresis phase of syphilis and in beri-beri, it was mapped by Korbinian Brodmann, and developed from the ectoderm of the gastrula. Its stem includes medulla and pons. Name this organ divided into telencephalon and diencephalon, quite large in humans, who frequently use it to think.
